_doc: CLINC-150 (D2) and emotion (D3) exposure audit written by shared/src/b02_clinc_overlap.py. counts[split] gives, for our 800 D2 test texts, the number of items with at least one matching row in that split: exact string, normalized (lower-case, punctuation removed, whitespace collapsed), near_dup_char (character 5-gram Jaccard >= 0.8 on normalized text) and near_dup_tok (word-set Jaccard >= 0.9); near-duplicate counts include exact and normalized matches, and *_in_scope / *_oos split them by our 600 in-scope and 200 out-of-scope items. Split keys are <variant>/<split> for the four oos-eval JSON files at commit 828f8093, hf_plus/<split> for clinc/clinc_oos config plus on the hub, and decider_temperature_fit_rows for the rebuilt 1500-row CLINC evaluation subsample decider-2b's temperature was fitted on. Test splits contain our items by construction, so they also have a *_other_rows entry that excludes the item's own row. emotion holds the same structure for the 498 d3_emotion items. card_quotes hold verbatim excerpts (quote) and our reading (note); hub_checks records what the Hugging Face hub publishes. In this public copy the emotion example texts (text, closest_char5, closest_token) are set to null because the dataset's terms do not grant redistribution; item_id identifies each example.

card_quotes.quote: "In-task" means the test splits of the training datasets; "held-out" means datasets never seen in training
Large label sets sub-sampled to 10 options; one temperature fitted on in-task data and stored in `decider_config.json`.
fine-tune it with cross-entropy, a proper scoring rule, on a mixture of about 95 public decision datasets
One epoch on a mixture of public decision datasets (intent detection, ticket routing, topic classification, sentiment, emotion, moderation, NLI, ...
Full label sets cost accuracy against 10 sampled options: CLINC 151-way 0.88 against 0.98
TRAIN_CAP = 20000     # per task / EVAL_CAP = 1500       # per task / SEED = 0; _sub(ds, n): ds.shuffle(seed=seed).select(range(n))
Post-hoc temperature is fitted on in-task data and tested on held-out tasks.
# temperature scaling: fit on in-task eval sets, report held-out

card_quotes.note: formats() builds this component from the training examples only (by_task is filled from `train`)
card_quotes.quote: wide        full native label sets (CLINC 151, Banking 77, ...)
Adapted from `decider-2b` (Apache-2.0) against a strictly proper scoring rule

card_quotes.note: the card's datasets field names only limberc/this-that-spatial-bench; no other training or temperature-fitting data is named and the decider-2b version adapted is not stated

card_quotes.quote: The whole adaptation is a single scalar λ applied as θ(λ) = θ₀ + λΔ

card_quotes.note: Neither card uses the words 'evaluation half'; the decider-2b card says the temperature was fitted on in-task data, which it defines as the test splits of the training datasets.

conclusion: Training exposure: decider-2b trains on clinc/clinc_oos plus train and dair-ai/emotion split train. Of our 800 D2 test texts, 0 occur verbatim, 5 after normalization, 20 as character 5-gram near-duplicates (Jaccard >= 0.8) and 12 as token near-duplicates (Jaccard >= 0.9) in that training split. Temperature-fitting exposure: decider-2b's card defines in-task data as the test splits of its training datasets and fits one temperature on it; the published loader keeps 1500 rows of clinc_oos plus test (shuffle seed 0). Rebuilding that subsample puts 201 of our 800 items inside it (160 in-scope, 41 out-of-scope; 218.2 expected by chance). This is established for the public loader code as released (core.py unchanged across its three commits) and the cached clinc_oos revision, and the label of every item inside agrees with its CLINC label. It cannot be established from public material that the released v10 temperature (1.3 in decider_config.json) was fitted with this exact code state and dataset revision, because the fitting run and its row list are not published. The fit pooled the in-task evaluation sets of all tasks (67 in the rebuilt regression set, at most 1500 rows each) with label sets sub-sampled to 10 options, so our items would enter one scalar temperature as a small share of the pool. The exposure concerns the stored temperature only: D2 accuracy does not depend on it, and the benchmark's scaled ECE for D2 refits T by five-fold cross-fitting on our items. this-that-model-1.0 is adapted from decider-2b and inherits the training exposure of the parent version it started from; its card names no other data, and it serves temperature 1.0 (no stored temperature), so decider-2b's temperature-fitting exposure does not carry over to its served probabilities. Neither training mixture is published on the hub (Mapika publishes only Mapika/decision-index-results); the one dataset this-that names, limberc/this-that-spatial-bench, is a grid and game-state benchmark with 0 D2 and 0 emotion text matches. Emotion: 30 of 498 d3_emotion items are verbatim in dair-ai/emotion split train (decider-2b training data), 32 counting character near-duplicates; 1 of 498 are in decider-2b's emotion temperature-fitting rows. All 498 item ids are row indices of dair-ai/emotion unsplit, the source of Ziems et al.'s test file, which is why a few items also fall in the split train, validation and test sets.

hub_checks.revision_note: the cached clinc_oos (155b9c71) and dair-ai/emotion (cab853a1) revisions are the heads of both repositories and date from 2024, before decider's code (2026-09-17), so a 2026 loader read the same row order that the rebuilt subsample uses
hub_checks.spatial_bench_note: normalized substring search of every D2 and emotion text longer than 15 characters in test.jsonl, the only data file

decider_temperature_fit_rows.core_py_history: three commits (81e154e3b5 2026-09-17, e3d97e5be0 2026-09-18, 751934af6f 2026-09-19); EVAL_CAP, SEED, _sub and the CLINC loader are identical in all three
decider_temperature_fit_rows.corroboration: eval_results.json in the Mapika/decider-2b snapshot d61c1c16 reports clinc_oos n = 1500, heldout = false
decider_temperature_fit_rows.rule: clinc/clinc_oos plus test, Dataset.shuffle(seed=0).select(range(1500)), as in Mapika/decider decider/data/core.py (_split_pair, _both, _sub; EVAL_CAP=1500, SEED=0)
decider_temperature_fit_rows.shuffle: Dataset.shuffle(seed) draws np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation, which is deterministic for a given row count
